questions.question: A unit annual life annuity-due is deferred to integer time $u>0$. It pays at times $u,u+1,\ldots$ while the recipient is alive. What happens to the annual dates $0,\ldots,u-1$ before payment begins?
options: Their missed payments are accumulated into a lump sum at time u.
Payments on those dates are made only if the recipient later reaches u.
Their payments occur at issue but use extra discounting.
No payments are earned on those earlier dates.

questions.question: A life alive at issue receives a unit annual annuity-due deferred $u$ integer years. What stream results when $u=0$?
options: The ordinary whole-life annuity-immediate stream, starting one year later.
The ordinary whole-life annuity-due stream, starting at issue.
A stream with no payments because the deferment interval is empty.
A single issue-date payment, with all later payments omitted.

questions.question: A life alive at issue buys a unit annual annuity-due whose first payment is at time $u>0$ years. Does the word due make that first future payment certain at issue?
options: Yes; every annuity-due has a certain first payment at issue.
Yes; only payments after time u require survival.
No; it still requires survival to time u.
No; the first payment instead requires death before time u.

questions.question: For integer deferment $u\ge0$, let $s=\mathbb{P}(T>u)>0$, $v>0$ be the annual discount factor, and $b$ the whole-life unit annuity-due APV at time u conditional on survival there. What factor transfers $b$ to its issue-date deferred APV?
options: $v^u s$.
$v^u/s$ when $s>0$.

questions.question: A unit annual annuity is deferred $u\ge1$ integer years. Compare its due version and its immediate version, both conditional on being alive at each payment date. Which pair gives their first payment dates?
options: Due at u-1; immediate at u.
Due at u; immediate also at u.
Due at u+1; immediate at u.
Due at u; immediate at u+1.

questions.question: A unit annual annuity-due is deferred three years and pays at each integer time $k\ge3$ only if future lifetime $T>k$. The realised lifetime is $T=4.7$ years. At which dates are payments made?
options: Times 3 and 4.
Times 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Times 4 and 5.
Time 3 only.

questions.question: A unit pension starts as an annual annuity-due at age $60$, provided a life currently aged $40$ survives. The actuarial transfer factor from issue to age $60$ is $E=0.3$, and the conditional annuity APV at age $60$ is $b=12$. What is its issue-date APV?
A unit whole-life annual annuity-due has APV $12$. Its temporary due prefix at times $0,\ldots,u-1$ has APV $8$ for integer $u>0$. What is the APV of the matching stream deferred to time u?
A unit annual annuity-due is deferred to time $u=2$ years. Its annual discount factor is $v=0.9$, and survival probability to time two is $0.8$. What is the APV of its first payment alone?

A unit-per-payment annual annuity-due deferred ten years has issue-date APV $3.6$. With the same deferment, mortality and interest, each retained payment is increased to $2$ units. What is the new APV?

For integer $u>0$, a deferred unit annuity-due has issue APV $D$ and finite positive conditional retirement APV $b$. Annual discount factor is $0<v<1$, and survival to retirement has positive probability. What bound on $D/b$ must hold across all such models?
options: $0<D/b\le v^u$.
$0<D/b\le1$, with no further restriction from deferment.
$D/b=v^u$ in every mortality model.
$D/b\ge v^u$.

questions.question: Fix a continuous lifetime $T$, discount factor $v>0$ and the original annual payment grid. Let $D_u$ be APV of unit payments at all integer times $k\ge u$ with $T>k$, and assume these APVs are finite. What happens as integer deferment u increases?
options: The APV must increase whenever v is greater than one.
The APV stays constant because its conditional retirement value includes one.
The APV cannot increase, even when v is greater than one.
The APV comparison requires the future annual survival probabilities to be equal.

questions.question: A unit annual annuity-due is deferred to integer time $u\ge1$, with positive discount factor $v$ and continuous lifetime $T$. Let $Y$ be its present value and $S(u)=\mathbb{P}(T>u)$. Which formula gives $\mathbb{P}(Y=0)$ in every such lifetime model?
options: Zero for every continuous lifetime model.

questions.question: A continuous lifetime has survival $S(2)=0.8,S(3)=0.4,S(4)=0$. A unit annual annuity-due starts at time two, and annual discount factor is $v=0.5$. What is its issue-date APV?
A future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $(0,4)$ years. At zero interest, a unit annual annuity-due pays from time two onwards only while alive. What is its APV?

On one original annual payment grid, unit whole-life due streams deferred to times two and five have issue APVs $D_2=5$ and $D_5=2$. What is the APV of unit payments only at times two, three and four, each requiring survival?

A continuous lifetime has zero probability of surviving to integer retirement time $u>0$. A unit annuity-due is defined by payments at integer dates $k\ge u$ only if $T>k$. What can be valued without defining a conditional model among retirement survivors?
options: Both original and survivor-conditioned retirement APVs must be zero.
The original APV is positive because the retirement annuity starts with one.
Its original-cohort APV is zero; the ordinary survivor-conditioned retirement value is not identified.
The original APV cannot be valued until a positive retirement survival probability is supplied.

questions.question: Two unit deferred annuities use transfer factors $E_1=0.3,E_2=0.6$ and finite conditional retirement annuity APVs $b_1=12,b_2=6$. Each issue APV is the product $E_jb_j$ for model $j=1,2$. What do these models show about equal deferred APVs?
options: Equal issue APVs do not identify each factor separately.
Equal issue APVs force equal transfer factors, $E_1=E_2$.
Equal issue APVs force equal retirement values, $b_1=b_2$.
A larger transfer factor always gives a larger issue APV.

questions.question: Unit annuity-due tails on one grid have quoted APVs $D_2=0.8296,D_3=0.5096,D_4=0.1$, and annual discount factor $v=0.8$. Each $D_u$ sums surviving payments at integer times $k\ge u$. Can these quotes arise from one continuous lifetime?
options: Yes; each later tail price is smaller than the preceding one.
No; the implied survival to time three exceeds survival to time two.
No; the implied survival probabilities sum to more than one.
Yes; each tail price is below the value of its corresponding certain perpetual stream.

questions.question: A life has continuous lifetime survivor $S(1)=0.8,S(2)=0.4,S(3)=0.1,S(4)=0$. Annual discount factor is $v=0.5$. A unit annuity-due starts at time one. Which pair gives its conditional time-one annuity APV $b$ and issue APV $D$?
